title: Senses of 'being able' (2): through faith
source_text: XII. Secundo, juxta eundem Doctorem, paulo propinquius dicimur, posse bene vivere, omnibusque tentationibus resistere, & peccata cavere per fidem, quamvis dilectione Dei, & actuali Dei adjutorio, internisque viribus voluntatis careamus. Nam quamvis fides ista omnia per se nullo modo possit, quia tamen est semen orationis, per quam charitatem & gratiam adjuvantem & voluntatis vires impetrare solemus, hinc per ipsam fidem ista posse dicimur.
pass_a_gloss: XII. Secondly, according to the same Doctor, somewhat nearer we are said to be able to live well, and to resist all temptations, and to avoid sins through faith, although we lack the love of God, and the actual help of God, and the inner strengths of the will. For although that faith can in no way do all these things by itself, yet because it is the seed of prayer, through which we are wont to obtain charity and assisting grace and strengths of the will, hence through faith itself we are said to be able to do these things.
pass_b_english: Thesis XII. Second, according to the same doctor, we are said, in a somewhat closer sense, to be able through faith to live rightly, withstand every temptation and avoid sins, even though we lack love for God, God's actual help and the will's inner strength.

Faith of itself cannot do any of this. But it is the seed of prayer, and by prayer we usually obtain love, helping grace and strength of will; that is why we are said to be able to do these things through faith itself.

choices.why: Caritas, the habitual theological virtue: 'love' in the reading, 'charity' in the literal pass.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
